I farm 20 mu in Quzhou, and I've been doing wheat-maize rotation here for a decade. My thinking is straightforward — I know this land, I know the local market prices, and with some family members working off-farm, I can't waste too much time on complicated management. I rely on my well for irrigation, which gives me more control than rain-fed farmers.

**Wheat (winter):** I'll plant all 20 mu with an improved variety — something like Jimai 22 or whatever the township station is recommending this year. I don't bother with traditional seed anymore; the yields just aren't there. I do rotary tillage after maize harvest to break up the stalks. I'll apply base fertilizer before sowing, then top-dress nitrogen at jointing. Three irrigations: one at sowing to get good emergence, one before winter sets in, one at jointing-heading. Two pesticide passes — herbicide in winter, then a fungicide-insecticide combo around heading when stripe rust and aphids show up. Expecting around 450 kg/mu if the weather cooperates.

**Maize (summer):** Right after wheat harvest in June I go straight to direct seeding — no-tillage saves me time and fuel. Hybrid seed,郑单958 type or similar. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, then side-dress urea at the big bell stage. Maize needs less babysitting than wheat. Two irrigations if it's dry — one at emergence, one at silking. One pesticide application early for corn borer. I'm targeting 550 kg/mu.

My priorities: keep input costs controlled because profit margins are tight, and keep labor manageable since the family isn't always available.
